raw: Act 4, Scene 5 — Juliet’s Chamber; Juliet on the bed
Enter Nurse.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Mistress! What, mistress! Juliet! Fast, I warrant her, she.
Why, lamb, why, lady, fie, you slug-abed!
Why, love, I say! Madam! Sweetheart! Why, bride!
What, not a word? You take your pennyworths now.
Sleep for a week; for the next night, I warrant,
The County Paris hath set up his rest
That you shall rest but little. God forgive me!
Marry and amen. How sound is she asleep!
I needs must wake her. Madam, madam, madam!
Ay, let the County take you in your bed,
He’ll fright you up, i’faith. Will it not be?
What, dress’d, and in your clothes, and down again?
I must needs wake you. Lady! Lady! Lady!
Alas, alas! Help, help! My lady’s dead!
O, well-a-day that ever I was born.
Some aqua vitae, ho! My lord! My lady!

gemma4_gloss.en: Madam!
What, madam!
Juliet!
I promise you, she is awake.
Why, lamb, why, lady, shame on you, you lazy sleeper!
Why, love, I say!
Madam!
Sweetheart!
Why, bride!
What, not a word?
You will take your coins now.
Sleep for a week.
For the next night, I promise, count Paris has prepared his place of rest that you will rest very little.
God forgive me!
Indeed and amen.
How deeply she is asleep!
I must wake her.
Madam, madam, madam!
Yes, let the Count take you in your bed.
He will frighten you awake, I believe.
Will it not be?
What, dressed and in your clothes, and then back down again?
I must wake you.
Lady!
Lady!
Lady!
Alas, alas!
Help, help!
My lady is dead!
Oh, what a day it is that I was ever born.
Some strong wine, quickly!
My lord!
My lady!

raw: Enter Lady Capulet.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: What noise is here?

gemma4_gloss.en: What noise is here?

speaker: NURSE
raw: O lamentable day!

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh, what a sad day!

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: What is the matter?

gemma4_gloss.en: What is the matter?

speaker: NURSE
raw: Look, look! O heavy day!

gemma4_gloss.en: Look, look!
Oh, what a sad day!

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
O me, O me! My child, my only life.
Revive, look up, or I will die with thee.
Help, help! Call help.

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh me, oh me!
My child, my only life.
Wake up, look up, or I will die with you.
Help, help!
Call for help.

raw: Enter Capulet.

speaker: CAPULET
raw: For shame, bring Juliet forth, her lord is come.

gemma4_gloss.en: For shame, bring Juliet out.
Her lord has arrived.

speaker: NURSE
raw: She’s dead, deceas’d, she’s dead; alack the day!

gemma4_gloss.en: She is dead, deceased, she is dead.
Oh no, what a day!

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: Alack the day, she’s dead, she’s dead, she’s dead!

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh no, the day!
She is dead.
She is dead.
She is dead!

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Ha! Let me see her. Out alas! She’s cold,
Her blood is settled and her joints are stiff.
Life and these lips have long been separated.
Death lies on her like an untimely frost
Upon the sweetest flower of all the field.

gemma4_gloss.en: Ha!
Let me see her.
Oh no!
She is cold.
Her blood has stopped moving and her joints are stiff.
Life and these lips have been apart for a long time.
Death lies on her like an early frost.
It is like frost on the sweetest flower in the field.

speaker: NURSE
raw: O lamentable day!

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh, what a sad day!

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: O woful time!

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh, what a miserable time!

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Death, that hath ta’en her hence to make me wail,
Ties up my tongue and will not let me speak.

gemma4_gloss.en: Death took her away to make me cry.
But death ties my tongue and will not let me speak.

raw: Enter Friar Lawrence and Paris with Musicians.

gemma4_gloss.en: Friar Lawrence and Paris enter with musicians.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: Come, is the bride ready to go to church?

gemma4_gloss.en: Come, is the bride ready to go to church?

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Ready to go, but never to return.
O son, the night before thy wedding day
Hath death lain with thy bride. There she lies,
Flower as she was, deflowered by him.
Death is my son-in-law, death is my heir;
My daughter he hath wedded. I will die
And leave him all; life, living, all is death’s.

gemma4_gloss.en: She is ready to go, but she will never return.
Oh son, death stayed with your bride the night before your wedding day.
There she lies.
She was like a flower, and he has ruined her.
Death is my son-in-law.
Death is my heir.
He has married my daughter.
I will die and leave everything to him.
Life, living, and all things belong to death.

speaker: PARIS
raw:
Have I thought long to see this morning’s face,
And doth it give me such a sight as this?

gemma4_gloss.en: Have I waited a long time to see this morning's face?
Does it give me such a sight as this?

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Accurs’d, unhappy, wretched, hateful day.
Most miserable hour that e’er time saw
In lasting labour of his pilgrimage.
But one, poor one, one poor and loving child,
But one thing to rejoice and solace in,
And cruel death hath catch’d it from my sight.

gemma4_gloss.en: Accursed, unhappy, wretched, hateful day.
This is the most miserable hour that time has ever seen.
But one, poor one, one poor and loving child.
There was only one thing to rejoice in and find comfort in.
Cruel death has taken it from my sight.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
O woe! O woeful, woeful, woeful day.
Most lamentable day, most woeful day
That ever, ever, I did yet behold!
O day, O day, O day, O hateful day.
Never was seen so black a day as this.
O woeful day, O woeful day.

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh woe! Oh woeful, woeful, woeful day.
Most lamentable day, most woeful day!
I have never seen such a sad day before.
Oh day, oh day, oh day, oh hateful day.
Never was such a black day seen as this.
Oh woeful day, oh woeful day.

speaker: PARIS
raw:
Beguil’d, divorced, wronged, spited, slain.
Most detestable death, by thee beguil’d,
By cruel, cruel thee quite overthrown.
O love! O life! Not life, but love in death!

gemma4_gloss.en: Betrayed, separated, wronged, insulted, killed.
Most detestable death, you have betrayed me.
Cruel, cruel death has completely overthrown me.
Oh love! Oh life!
Not life, but love in death!

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Despis’d, distressed, hated, martyr’d, kill’d.
Uncomfortable time, why cam’st thou now
To murder, murder our solemnity?
O child! O child! My soul, and not my child,
Dead art thou. Alack, my child is dead,
And with my child my joys are buried.

gemma4_gloss.en: Despised, distressed, hated, martyred, killed.
Uncomfortable time, why did you come now?
Why do you murder our solemnity?
Oh child! Oh child!
My soul, and not my child, is dead.
Oh no, my child is dead.
My joys are buried with my child.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Peace, ho, for shame. Confusion’s cure lives not
In these confusions. Heaven and yourself
Had part in this fair maid, now heaven hath all,
And all the better is it for the maid.
Your part in her you could not keep from death,
But heaven keeps his part in eternal life.
The most you sought was her promotion,
For ’twas your heaven she should be advanc’d,
And weep ye now, seeing she is advanc’d
Above the clouds, as high as heaven itself?
O, in this love, you love your child so ill
That you run mad, seeing that she is well.
She’s not well married that lives married long,
But she’s best married that dies married young.
Dry up your tears, and stick your rosemary
On this fair corse, and, as the custom is,
And in her best array bear her to church;
For though fond nature bids us all lament,
Yet nature’s tears are reason’s merriment.

gemma4_gloss.en: Peace, stop this. Confusion does not cure confusion.
Heaven and you both had a part in this fair maid.
Now heaven has everything.
It is better for the maid this way.
You could not keep your part in her from death.
But heaven keeps its part in eternal life.
The most you wanted was her promotion.
She should have been promoted to heaven.
Why do you weep now that she is advanced?
She is above the clouds, as high as heaven itself.
In this love, you love your child so poorly.
You are running mad because you see that she is well.
She is not well married if she lives married long.
But she is best married if she dies married young.
Dry your tears.
Put your rosemary on this fair body.
Follow the custom and carry her to church in her best clothes.
Although foolish nature tells us all to lament, nature's tears are reason's joy.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
All things that we ordained festival
Turn from their office to black funeral:
Our instruments to melancholy bells,
Our wedding cheer to a sad burial feast;
Our solemn hymns to sullen dirges change;
Our bridal flowers serve for a buried corse,
And all things change them to the contrary.

gemma4_gloss.en: All things that we planned as a festival turn into a black funeral.
Our instruments become melancholy bells.
Our wedding cheer becomes a sad burial feast.
Our solemn hymns change to sad songs for the dead.
Our bridal flowers are used for a buried body.
Everything has changed to the opposite.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Sir, go you in, and, madam, go with him,
And go, Sir Paris, everyone prepare
To follow this fair corse unto her grave.
The heavens do lower upon you for some ill;
Move them no more by crossing their high will.

gemma4_gloss.en: Sir, go in.
Madam, go with him.
Sir Paris, everyone prepare to follow this fair body to her grave.
The heavens are lowering upon you for some evil.
Do not move them more by going against their high will.

raw: Exeunt Capulet, Lady Capulet, Paris and Friar.

gemma4_gloss.en: Capulet, Lady Capulet, Paris, and the Friar leave.

speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
raw: Faith, we may put up our pipes and be gone.

gemma4_gloss.en: I believe we can stop playing our pipes and leave now.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Honest good fellows, ah, put up, put up,
For well you know this is a pitiful case.

gemma4_gloss.en: Good men, please stop.
Stop now.
You know well that this is a sad case.

speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
raw: Ay, by my troth, the case may be amended.

gemma4_gloss.en: Yes, I believe the situation can be improved.

raw: Exit Nurse.
Enter Peter.

speaker: PETER
raw:
Musicians, O, musicians, ‘Heart’s ease,’ ‘Heart’s ease’, O, and you
will have me live, play ‘Heart’s ease.’

gemma4_gloss.en: Musicians, oh, musicians!
Play 'Heart's ease'.
Play 'Heart's ease'!
You will let me live.
Play 'Heart's ease'.

speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
raw: Why ‘Heart’s ease’?

gemma4_gloss.en: Why 'Heart's ease'?

speaker: PETER
raw:
O musicians, because my heart itself plays ‘My heart is full’. O play
me some merry dump to comfort me.

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh musicians, because my heart plays 'My heart is full'.
Play some happy music to comfort me.

speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
raw: Not a dump we, ’tis no time to play now.

gemma4_gloss.en: We will not play a dance.
It is not the time to play now.

speaker: PETER
raw: You will not then?

gemma4_gloss.en: Will you not then?

speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
raw: No.

gemma4_gloss.en: No.

speaker: PETER
raw: I will then give it you soundly.

gemma4_gloss.en: I will give it to you strongly then.

speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
raw: What will you give us?

gemma4_gloss.en: What will you give us?

speaker: PETER
raw: No money, on my faith, but the gleek! I will give you the minstrel.

gemma4_gloss.en: I have no money, I promise.
But I will give you the gleek!
I will give you the minstrel.

speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
raw: Then will I give you the serving-creature.

gemma4_gloss.en: Then I will give you the servant.

speaker: PETER
raw:
Then will I lay the serving-creature’s dagger on your pate. I will
carry no crotchets. I’ll re you, I’ll fa you. Do you note me?

gemma4_gloss.en: Then I will put the servant's dagger on your head.
I do not carry any notes.
I will play you. I will strike you.
Do you understand me?

speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
raw: And you re us and fa us, you note us.

gemma4_gloss.en: And you play us and strike us.
You understand us.

speaker: SECOND MUSICIAN
raw: Pray you put up your dagger, and put out your wit.

gemma4_gloss.en: Please put away your dagger.
Stop using your cleverness.

speaker: PETER
raw:
Then have at you with my wit. I will dry-beat you with an iron wit, and
put up my iron dagger. Answer me like men.
‘When griping griefs the heart doth wound,
And doleful dumps the mind oppress,
Then music with her silver sound’—
Why ‘silver sound’? Why ‘music with her silver sound’? What say you,
Simon Catling?

gemma4_gloss.en: Then use your intelligence against me.
I will beat you with an iron wit.
I will put away my iron dagger.
Answer me like men.
When painful sorrows wound the heart, and sad feelings weigh down the mind, then music with her silver sound why 'silver sound'?
Why 'music with her silver sound'?
What do you say, Simon Catling?

speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
raw: Marry, sir, because silver hath a sweet sound.

gemma4_gloss.en: Indeed, sir, because silver has a sweet sound.

speaker: PETER
raw: Prates. What say you, Hugh Rebeck?

gemma4_gloss.en: You are just talking. What do you say, Hugh Rebeck?

speaker: SECOND MUSICIAN
raw: I say ‘silver sound’ because musicians sound for silver.

gemma4_gloss.en: I say 'silver sound' because musicians play for silver.

speaker: PETER
raw: Prates too! What say you, James Soundpost?

gemma4_gloss.en: You are also just talking! What do you say, James Soundpost?

speaker: THIRD MUSICIAN
raw: Faith, I know not what to say.

gemma4_gloss.en: Truly, I do not know what to say.

speaker: PETER
raw:
O, I cry you mercy, you are the singer. I will say for you. It is
‘music with her silver sound’ because musicians have no gold for
sounding.
‘Then music with her silver sound
With speedy help doth lend redress.’

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh, I beg your mercy.
You are the singer.
I will speak for you.
It is 'music with her silver sound' because musicians have no gold for playing.
Then music with her silver sound with speedy help gives relief.

raw: Exit.

speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
raw: What a pestilent knave is this same!

gemma4_gloss.en: What a disgusting man this one is!

speaker: SECOND MUSICIAN
raw:
Hang him, Jack. Come, we’ll in here, tarry for the mourners, and stay
dinner.

gemma4_gloss.en: Hang him, Jack.
Come, let's go inside.
We will wait for the mourners.
And we will stay for dinner.
